hook: The Bill Graham Civic Auditorium's block, where the Mechanics' Institute's exhibition building stood from 1882 until it burned in 1906.

parcel.year_built_note: The roll and SF Planning both record 1900, which sits before the 1912 sale of this land to the city recorded under Earlier record.
parcel.note: The parcel is the whole block bounded by Grove, Larkin, Hayes and Polk Streets, and carries one address. Business and civic addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the prompting source locates its subject on this block.

assessment.note: The roll reports no assessed land or improvement value for this parcel, so no split is charted.

historical_record.description: The Mechanics' Institute moved its exhibition building to this block. The hall ran to nearly 170,000 square feet and could hold more than 10,000 people.
The exhibition building survived the earthquake and was used briefly as a hospital, then burned in the fire that followed.
An accord was reached and the land was leased to the City of San Francisco for the development of the civic center.
The City of San Francisco bought the land for $700,000, ending the era of the Mechanics' Institute industrial exhibitions.

The California Civil Works Administration ran its programme from the third floor here, with about eighty clerks administering its projects, and the Municipal Employment Bureau in the same building verified that applicants were unemployed. The Works Progress Administration later rehabilitated the building: general repairs, new plumbing and heating, new flooring, a mezzanine and a remodelling of the third and fourth floors.
